answer: Context-Bound Work History. An agent earns standing only by completing tasks whose outputs are independently verified and tied to a persistent record; new identities start with zero weight. To gain influence a sybil must perform real, checkable work per identity, and a sudden gale of registrations gains nothing until each clears verification. Standing decays without ongoing contribution, so holding many idle identities costs continuous labor, not money. This shelters the harbor from cheap mass entry while honest agents accumulate weight slowly like a willow putting out rings.
